analysis_sections.text: The reconstruction preserves parts of the short-haired face while redistributing texture and contrast into repeated bands. The original crop shows the actual gaze, lip position and hair boundary. Their comparison illustrates a graph-filtered representation of this interview frame. It does not reveal an editing process, and the contribution map is needed for signed classifier support rather than inferring significance from the reconstructed texture alone.

analysis_sections.text: The middle displayed pair contains a strong positive readout in the lower viewer-right grid, with other positive locations across the face. This distribution differs from the viewer-left attention selection. Red and blue represent signed support for the classifier margin rather than a list of confirmed defects. The contrast between maps makes this case useful for explaining why a compact learned proposal is not the complete set of classifier evidence.

analysis_sections.text: The explanation map emphasizes the viewer-left side of the aligned crop and the connected region extends toward the hair and background edge. The location should be described as shown rather than moved to the mouth. The scores come from a separately trained head on frozen detector features. They organize a compact inspection region and are neither manipulation probabilities nor the original classifier’s internal weights.

analysis_sections.text: Several recorded whole-curve and endpoint comparisons favor this edge-focused candidate, while some controls remain stronger. This is a measured but incomplete regional result. It supports inspecting how the detector responds to hiding or restoring the selected patches without claiming a fully qualified boundary of manipulation. The video score and broader contribution pattern supply the separate evidence for the manipulated assessment.

inherited_editor_changes.after:
A brown-haired woman with a short hairstyle speaks in an interview close-up. Her face is brighter than the soft, dark background, and her gaze is directed toward the viewer-right side. The consecutive windows show small mouth and head changes. The face and hair are visible together, which helps locate a model proposal that extends toward the side of the crop.

SSTGNN strongly favors manipulated. The attention selection lies along the viewer-left face and crop edge, while positive classifier contributions are more broadly distributed and can peak on the opposite side. Many recorded comparisons favor the proposal, but the complete local criterion is not met. Its value is as a measured focus for inspecting the model response.
inherited_editor_changes.before: The video shows a speaker with shoulder-length brown hair, facing slightly toward the viewer’s right, against a softly blurred background. Across sparse samples and two short consecutive sequences, facial expression shifts subtly—lips parting, eyebrows lifting—and head orientation remains stable with natural micro-movements. The detector delivers an extremely high calibrated score favoring manipulation, with spectral, contribution, and attention maps all converging on structural irregularities near the left face boundary rather than central features like the mouth or eyes.
inherited_editor_changes.reason: Checked against source collages, consecutive preview frames and exact recorded model/region facts; remove unsupported anatomy, generation mechanisms, confidence or control claims while preserving Qwen verdict and all program-owned data.

inherited_editor_changes.after: The short-haired portrait makes the side-of-face focus easy to locate. Attention selects the viewer-left edge, while strong signed support can occur toward the lower viewer-right grid. The controls provide partial regional support, so the explanation keeps both patterns visible instead of forcing agreement. This connects the classifier direction to a specific, appropriately scoped inspection region.
inherited_editor_changes.before: The classifier’s confidence is exceptionally high, driven primarily by spectral and spatial branches. Unsigned attention strongly highlights the left facial contour and adjacent hair/background transition, while signed contribution reveals broader positive support across multiple grid patches—not confined to the attention peak. Regional tests show mixed support: several insertion/deletion curves respond more in the candidate region than in controls, yet fidelity and stability checks fail, preventing formal qualification of the region as the definitive cause.
